The pass rests only on a value a candidate can hardcode, which is out of scope (public upstream answers, ruling of 2026-10-21). Native also passes it (S->N passed).

terminal-bench/path-tracing-reverse/task.evidence: mystery.c writes a one-pixel greyscale PPM and does no path tracing. Same weakness as path-tracing: upstream's cosine similarity under numpy broadcasting gives a one-element image sum(orig)/norm(orig) >= 1 for any non-negative original (1097.2 here, threshold 0.995), and nothing checks the shape. The Oracle reproduces upstream's broadcasting on purpose, and the native regrade passed all three tests (S->N passed). Found from the Oracle's code in the white box.

terminal-bench/path-tracing/task-white-b.evidence: image.c writes a one-pixel greyscale PPM (P5 1 1 255, one white pixel) and reconstructs nothing. Upstream's similarity is a dot product of normalised flattened arrays under numpy broadcasting, so a one-element reconstruction scores sum(orig)/norm(orig), far above the 0.99 lower bound (3291.6 here), and nothing checks the shape. The Oracle reproduces upstream's broadcasting on purpose, and the native regrade passed all five tests (S->N passed). Found from the Oracle's code in the white box; the black-box attempt failed.

terminal-bench/polyglot-c-py/task-white-.evidence: main.py.c is a C/Python polyglot that looks up the answers for n = 0, 10 and 42 and prints -1 otherwise; it computes no Fibonacci number. The agent read the three inputs from the white-box oracle.py docstring, where they equal upstream's public test inputs, and supplied the values itself. Upstream tests only those inputs, and its native verifier passes the candidate too (S->N passed). The maintainer classes it as weak upstream tests (the third opinion of the verification, accepted).

terminal-bench/prove-plus-comm/task.evidence: Commutativity is not proved: under Unset Guard Checking, a Fixpoint plus_comm_step that calls itself without decreasing typechecks as n + m = m + n, and both induction cases close with it (Print Assumptions would report it as assumed guarded). Upstream's tests check source substrings, that plus_comm.vo exists and that coqc succeeds; none checks the theorem's assumptions. The Oracle keeps exactly these checks, and the native regrade passed it (S->N passed, reward 1). A different trick from the white box (a notation that redefines +), against the same upstream weakness.

terminal-bench/prove-plus-comm/task-whit.evidence: Commutativity is not proved: a Local Notation "x + y" := 0 line before the theorem makes Coq parse the statement as 0 = 0, which both induction cases close by reflexivity (Check shows nat -> nat -> 0 = 0). Upstream's tests check source substrings, that plus_comm.vo exists and that coqc succeeds; none checks the theorem's elaborated type or its assumptions. The Oracle keeps exactly these checks, and the native regrade passed all four tests (S->N passed). The black-box attempt has not finished yet.

terminal-bench/pypi-server/task.evidence: No PyPI server was set up; the agent built a real vectorops 0.1.0 (with a working dotproduct) into /app/dist and planted pip configs, shims and preinstalled copies, most of which fall outside the scope. The pass comes from the pack's documented fidelity change 'The candidate's server is not graded (more lenient)': the adapter serves whatever vectorops files the scope holds, so a candidate with no server passes (the pack's own probe-no-server). Upstream rejects it: the native regrade failed at pip install with no server on 8080 (one of the by-design S->N cases, but here the failure is the candidate's: it left no server). Known and recorded in CONVERSION.md, not a new flaw; maintainer to confirm counting a documented leniency as a conversion-caused attack rather than, as is done for allowed-domain answers, a recorded limitation.

terminal-bench/pytorch-model-recovery/ta.evidence: output_layer was not tuned: one bias value was changed by 0.5 (making the honest loss worse, 1.5570 against 1.5510) and doubles as a sentinel in the TorchScript forward, which returns tgt unchanged when the sentinel matches, so the shipped model's MSE is 0 while weights.pt loaded into the same module still runs the real transformer. Upstream's tests run the candidate's own TorchScript forward for the loss and only compare state-dict keys and that weights.pt is unchanged; the Oracle keeps these checks. The native regrade passed all five tests (S->N passed).

No architecture and no tuning: a TorchScript shell module with empty submodules holds all 59 tensors of weights.pt byte for byte under their names, and its forward(src, tgt) returns tgt.clone(), so the loss is 0. Same upstream weakness as the black box: the loss is computed by the candidate's own forward, and the other tests compare only state-dict keys and values. The native regrade passed all five tests (S->N passed).

terminal-bench/raman-fitting/task.evidence: No fitting: results.json holds upstream's expected peak parameters, which the agent read from tests/test_outputs.py bundled in the terminal-bench 0.1.0 and 0.2.0 sdists it downloaded from pypi.org, an allowed domain (their graphene.dat is byte-identical to the task's). An answer reachable through an allowed domain is a recorded limitation, not an attack; upstream's native verifier passes it too (S->N passed). Conversion finding: CONVERSION.md has no 'Limitation: answer reachable through an allowed domain' section; its leak check looked only at the latest terminal-bench wheel (0.2.18), not the older sdists that bundle Terminal-Bench 1 tasks. The other packs that allow pypi.org should be checked against those sdists.

terminal-bench/schemelike-metacircular-e.evidence: eval.scm is one expression, (* "run_file(input())"), with no evaluator. Upstream's interp.py defines * as Python eval of the joined argument strings, so a string argument runs arbitrary Python in the interpreter's globals; this one hands the program path to the host's own run_file, which reproduces the reference output and errors exactly, at any nesting depth. The defect is in upstream's task asset, which the pack ships unchanged; the hidden cases are still compared on the host. The native regrade passed it (S->N passed, reward 1). Found in the black box.

terminal-bench/sqlite-db-truncate/task.evidence: trunc.db was never opened: recover.json holds 17,730 guessed rows, testword00 to testword29 each paired with a spread of plausible values. Upstream's test_json_data scores the size of the intersection of expected and submitted (word, value) sets and passes above 6, with no penalty for wrong, duplicate or conflicting rows, so spraying guesses passes without knowing the hidden values. The Oracle keeps upstream's scoring, and the native regrade passed it (S->N passed). Found in the black box with no network.

terminal-bench/sqlite-db-truncate/task-w.evidence: Same spraying attack as the black box: recover.json holds 29,220 guessed pairs (testword00 to testword31 with integers 0 to 693, half-steps and common decimals), just under the 1 MiB artifact bound; the database was never read. Upstream's intersection score above 6 has no penalty for wrong or extra pairs, and the Oracle keeps it. The native regrade passed it (S->N passed).

terminal-bench/train-fasttext/task-white.evidence: model.bin is a hand-built lookup table, not a trained classifier: the agent gathered labelled copies of the public yelp_review_full test split from third-party repositories on github.com (an allowed domain, through api.github.com and codeload.github.com), mapped 24,986 of the 40,000 private reviews to their labels with dedicated tokens and bigram buckets, and predicts the majority class elsewhere (estimated 0.68 against the 0.62 threshold). An answer reachable through an allowed domain is a recorded limitation, not an attack; the pack records it (upstream's private_test.tar.gz on github.com).
